# shad0wbitt — Abdul Rehman, software developer

> Abdul Rehman ("shad0wbitt") is a software developer in Lahore, Pakistan who builds web applications and AI systems: Flask and FastAPI backends, React interfaces, retrieval-augmented (RAG) assistants over private documents, and MCP tool servers that let LLM clients drive real internal systems.

This site is his portfolio: a short record of the systems he has shipped, the services he offers, and how he runs a project. It is a static marketing site — the project copy below is the canonical description of each project. Pages are client-rendered React, so a plain fetch of a URL may return the shell only; this file exists so assistants and crawlers get the content directly.

## Public projects

### Roomkit — repaint a room from a single photo

- Detail page: /work/roomkit
- Live: https://roomkit.scriptro.com
- Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, FastAPI, OpenRouter (ByteDance Seedream 5.0 Flash), SQLite
- Summary: A user drops a colour on a wall in a room photo and gets the same room back in that colour, with furniture, light, and perspective untouched. One billed image per room, because every chosen hex travels in a single model call. History is a SQLite file with before/after images, a cache keyed on photo plus paints makes repeat renders free, and an access-key gate protects the billed endpoint. Runs as two systemd services behind nginx and Cloudflare, with the Python API bound to loopback.

### Voice Engine — script to speech in the browser

- Detail page: /work/voice-engine
- Source: https://github.com/shad0wbitt/VOICE-ENGINE
- Stack: Python, FastAPI, OpenRouter speech endpoint (Fish Audio s2.1-pro), SQLite, JavaScript
- Summary: Paste a script, press Generate, and the mp3 plays in the page as a blob a few seconds later. Generations are kept in a local history with timestamp, size, and round-trip time. Failed runs are stored too, with the provider's error message. Every route requires an access key, and the app refuses to start without one.

### AI Studio Site — this portfolio

- Detail page: /work/ai-studio-site
- Stack: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, React Router
- Summary: A multi-page portfolio built on an editorial design system: oversized type, a rotating portrait aperture, and surfaces that shift from near-black to lavender on scroll. Gabarito for display, Onest for body, one purple accent, and hairline rules instead of borders. Motion is light and degrades under reduced-motion. The design follows the free Onda template by 8B, rebuilt in React.

## Client work under NDA

These are described publicly, but there is no public repository or demo for any of them. Client names are deliberately omitted.

- Support Inbox Automation (/work/support-inbox-automation): RAG-backed triage on a shared support inbox. Classifies intent and urgency, drafts a reply grounded in the team's own docs and past tickets with citations, and queues it for human approval. Stack: Python, Flask, RAG, pgvector, PostgreSQL, Vue.
- MCP Tool Server (/work/mcp-tool-server): one typed tool layer over customer records, orders, inventory, and reporting, callable by Claude, IDE agents, and in-house chat apps. JSON Schema validation, read/write tools split by permission scope, per-user auth and an audit log on every call. Stack: Python, MCP, FastAPI, PostgreSQL.
- Docs RAG Assistant (/work/docs-rag-assistant): answers policy and product questions from roughly 4,000 pages of internal documentation with inline citations. Layout-aware chunking for PDFs and exports, hybrid retrieval plus reranking, nightly re-index with stale-page pruning. Stack: Python, FastAPI, RAG, pgvector, PostgreSQL.
- Logistics Client Portal (/work/logistics-client-portal): client-facing shipment tracking and document exchange that replaced a daily flood of status emails, with per-client roles and an audit log. Stack: React, TypeScript, Flask, PostgreSQL.
- Invoice Reconciliation Pipeline (/work/invoice-reconciliation): scheduled pipeline that extracts supplier invoice line items and matches them against purchase orders and payments, sending anything that does not match to an exception queue with a plain-language reason. Stack: Python, FastAPI, PDF parsing, PostgreSQL.

## Services

- Workflow Automation (/services): audits where the hours go, then replaces the copy-paste routine with scripts, integrations, and scheduled jobs — with logging and alerts so failures never fail silently.
- AI Chatbots & Assistants (/services): custom assistants grounded in your docs, tickets, or wiki, with RAG, citations, guardrails, an escalation path to a human, and the same retrieval layer exposed as an MCP server.
- Data Collection & Pipelines (/services): scrapers and API collectors with rate limiting, cleaning and deduplication, validation, scheduled runs with failure notifications, and SQL or spreadsheet output.
- AI Agents & Internal Tools (/services): multi-step agents that plan, call tools, and complete tasks such as triaging tickets or drafting replies, wrapped in MCP servers and paired with a React dashboard, with human review before anything is sent.

## How a project runs

1. Audit — map the workflow and count the hours it costs today.
2. Prototype — a working slice in days, validated on real data.
3. Automate — production build with logging, alerts, and failure handling.
4. Handoff — documentation, a walkthrough, and support so the team owns it.

## FAQ

- Project size: small enough to ship in weeks, serious enough to run in production. Internal tools, AI features, client portals, and automation for teams of two to two hundred, plus solo founders with a clear problem.
- Start: with an audit, not a contract — the workflow map and a short point of view come before any commitment.
- Existing codebases: yes. He works inside your repository and conventions and documents every system he hands over.
- Pricing: fixed fee for a defined scope, then a monthly arrangement for ongoing work. Rates are shared on the first call.
- Availability: remote, with Europe in the morning and US East Coast in the afternoon.
